title: Exact-v6 ChipState Deep CFR adapter smoke
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: A minimal external-sampling CFR traversal can operate directly on the audited physical-v6 ChipState/action table with stable nine-slot information sets, no opponent-hole leakage, exact zero-sum payoffs, and bounded deterministic smoke traversals.
material_change: Add a physical-v6 56D information-set encoder and nine-slot external-sampling traversal that use ChipState and policy_contract_v6.action_table directly; do not modify the legacy Deep CFR rules engine.
baseline: The readiness audit rejected the legacy HUNL integration on all five contract gates while confirming tabular Leduc convergence to 26.1112 mbb/game.
notes: Adapter/mechanism smoke only. Root traversals are not claimed as environment training hands and no weights are optimized.

result.summary: The direct ChipState external-sampling adapter passed every mechanism gate on 16 unique alternating-seat roots: 48,016 decisions, 37,352 terminal rollouts, 2,672 finite masked targets per traverser, exact shared action slots/transitions, zero-sum BB payoffs, and opponent-hole encoding invariance.
result.conclusion: Exact physical-v6 CFR traversal is feasible without the legacy HUNL rules engine. The evidence admits a bounded neural regret optimization smoke, but does not yet establish learning quality or count as environment training hands.
result.next_step: Run a deterministic small neural-regret optimization with explicit root-deal/node accounting; require healthy target/loss distributions, checkpoint reload parity, nontrivial behavioral movement, and untouched evaluation against fixed exact-v6 policies before scaling.
